# PR 293 correctness review, round 1

Head: d17dae35a62fd7fbf88a17f230a0603d77fafdc4
Base: 288d0d078fe0ef524a3e56c87a94ae8f6a382d88
Request: 01a1f956-da41-73d2-8980-b5c4cbd6d827
Reviewer: pij-sufficient-clam

## A. Verdict

BLOCK: P293-001. The new pre-SIGINT tmux command has no deadline.
The review worktree remains read-only, and reviewer/293 stays held until merge.

## B. Summary

The HTTP stream wedge and release ordering are fixed at this head. The release
is launched before the joins; the live-client teardown runs outside its state
mutex, and a read waits for its reply outside that mutex. The released flag
prevents a subsequent read from starting another control client.

The HTTP listener stops accepting, graceful requests receive the fixed drain,
and the sole watch sender is dropped after the drain. Remaining connection
futures then drop their sockets. This is a TCP EOF witness, not a promise of
successful HTTP body completion or automatic CLI reconnection.

## C. Findings

| ID | Severity | Location | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| P293-001 | HIGH | justfile:746-756 | Bound the new tmux helper before SIGINT. |
| N293-001 | Nonblocking inherited limit | crates/cli/src/main.rs:2276-2306; docs/how/pij-rs-api.md:166-172 | CLI tail exits on stream EOF/error; do not claim all streaming clients reconnect. |

## D. Blocking reproduction

The exact added pre-signal block was extracted from the reviewed justfile and
run against a newly created private tmux server. Only that server's recorded
PID was stopped. A marker stood in for the daemon signal; no live daemon was
signalled.

With the private server frozen, the helper remained pending after 2.010 s and
the signal marker had not run. Resuming that server allowed set-option to
finish, and only then did the marker run. A frozen server can therefore hold
the bounce indefinitely before its existing 30 s post-signal deadline starts.
The private server was resumed and removed.

Round 2 should bound the helper, clean up only the helper process it owns, and
make the timeout disposition explicit: signal after a diagnosed best-effort
failure, or refuse the bounce without falsely claiming the protection ran.

## E. Proof ceilings and preserved behavior

- Early release: crates/daemon/src/lib.rs:359-407;
  crates/tmux/src/control.rs:477-482,494-566. Teardown is outside the adapter
  state mutex; query reply waiting is also outside it. The permanent released
  adapter test verifies that later reads do not reattach.
- HTTP drain: crates/daemon/src/serve.rs:44-95; both daemon listeners receive
  SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT. The open-stream test reads raw TCP EOF; the slow
  request test finishes inside the drain. Workers/control joins retain their
  existing timing properties, so HTTP <= 5 s plus store drain <= 5 s is not
  a universal bound on the entire shutdown.
  The cutoff is a policy: it decides to drop connections after the grace.
  The pre-signal tmux option is a brake: it can only spare `_pij` on client exit.
- Admitted writes: crates/store/src/migrate.rs:43-56 owns store writes across
  caller cancellation; events/mod.rs:99-172 retains the publication guard;
  delivery/mod.rs:1229-1269 owns delivery continuation and compensation.
  The existing cancellation tests establish commit/publication ownership.
  They are not an exhaustive proof of every filesystem/external side effect.
  Work not admitted before cancellation may never run; completion past the
  final store-drain deadline is not promised.
- OMP event supervision retries both normal stream completion and errors
  (daemon-http.ts:374-451); its cursor/key-refresh fixture is covered by
  exact-head CI. Native Copilot receives through its existing retrying inbox
  loop; its local node:test contracts passed.
- Tail's exit on EOF/error predates this PR: the baseline SIGKILL also ended
  the connection. It is not a newly introduced correctness block.
- Cost: the watch/select adds O(open connections) memory/poll work without a
  new connection task or daemon launch site. Release is once per stop; the
  helper is one process per bounce; post-release reads use existing fork
  sites. Performance owns live before/after receipts. No live bounce was run.
- Socket/environment security is owned by security/293. A source-verified
  explicit -S ownership-check candidate was handed to that holder with its
  unverified limits; this correctness review does not substitute a security
  verdict or a two-user reproduction.

## F. Commands and results

All cargo commands used just shared-build, its one shared target/lock,
niceness 19 and four jobs. No node_modules was installed or symlinked.

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| just pr-freeze 293 | FINAL at the requested full head; all latest CI jobs passed. |
| git diff --check 288d0d07 d17dae35 | Passed. |
| shared-build: test -p pij-daemon --lib serve::tests -- --nocapture | Passed: 5 tests, 2.02 s test runtime. |
| shared-build: test -p pij-cli --test daemon_stop -- --nocapture | Passed: 1 test, 5.89 s including fixture boot. |
| shared-build: test -p pij-tmux --test control_teardown a_released_adapter_leaves_through_its_teardown_and_never_reattaches -- --nocapture | Passed: 1 test, 0.15 s. |
| shared-build: clippy -p pij-daemon -p pij-cli -p pij-tmux --all-targets -- -D warnings | Passed on macOS. |
| Ordering mutation: release moved after tokio::join!, test -p pij-cli --test daemon_stop -- --nocapture | CAUGHT: exit 101, `_pij was not handled while the stream was open`. |
| Unbounded-drain mutation: test -p pij-daemon --lib serve::tests::an_open_stream_does_not_hold_the_stop -- --nocapture | CAUGHT: exit 101, `the stop is not held by the stream: Elapsed(())`, 7.01 s. |
| shared-build: test -p pij-store --test cancellation -- --nocapture | Passed: 1 test, including caller abort and timeout, 0.07 s. |
| shared-build: test -p pij-daemon --lib events::governance_cancellation_tests -- --nocapture | Passed: 4 tests, 0.23 s. |
| shared-build: build --locked -p pij-cli --bin pij-rs | Passed after the mutation runs, restoring the shared debug binary from the exact reviewed head; no install or live restart. |
| harness boot | NOT-READY advisory: linked-worktree dependencies absent. |
| harness checks --quick | Exit 1: local TS tools missing / ambient Biome incompatible; native Copilot, SDK contract and pij-skill stages passed. Heavy stages skipped. Exact-head CI supplies TS proof under C25. |

Local review receipt filenames: pr293-focused-tests.log,
pr293-mutation-ordering.log, pr293-mutation-drain.log,
pr293-cancellation-tests.log, pr293-bounce-stall.log,
pr293-harness-checks.log.

Exact baseline command:

```bash
PIJ_SHARED_TARGET="$(harness/scripts/cargo-target.sh)" just shared-build -- test -p pij-daemon --lib serve::tests -- --nocapture --then test -p pij-cli --test daemon_stop -- --nocapture --then test -p pij-tmux --test control_teardown a_released_adapter_leaves_through_its_teardown_and_never_reattaches -- --nocapture --then clippy -p pij-daemon -p pij-cli -p pij-tmux --all-targets -- -D warnings
```

Exact cancellation command:

```bash
PIJ_SHARED_TARGET="$(harness/scripts/cargo-target.sh)" just shared-build -- test -p pij-store --test cancellation -- --nocapture --then test -p pij-daemon --lib events::governance_cancellation_tests -- --nocapture
```

Mutation commands ran only in the isolated committed-source archive:

```bash
PIJ_SHARED_TARGET=<checkout-target> just shared-build -- test -p pij-cli --test daemon_stop -- --nocapture
PIJ_SHARED_TARGET=<checkout-target> just shared-build -- test -p pij-daemon --lib serve::tests::an_open_stream_does_not_hold_the_stop -- --nocapture
```

## G. Harness feedback

magicWand: a permanent pre-signal timeout fixture that proves the stop deadline
begins before any potentially blocking helper.

difficulties:
- degrading: checks in a dependency-free review worktree invoke missing local
  TS tools and an incompatible ambient formatter instead of returning the
  dependency-not-ready advisory that boot already exposes.
- annoying: raw TCP EOF tests cannot establish actual CLI tail reconnection;
  the client's inherited exit behavior must be distinguished from extension
  supervision and from a complete HTTP response.

Captured in the reviewer-specific harness observation bucket. Encode the
timeout fixture with the round-2 fix; do not expand this PR into new shutdown
machinery or unrelated client changes.

## H. Handover

PM already routed P293-001 to the coder for round 2. Re-review only the helper
deadline/failure disposition and security holder's requested repairs at the
new exact head. The prime owns the first postmerge bounce of the old daemon
and the second bounce proving the new shutdown. Reviewer holding remains.
